BLOCKING for AC-8, found by wave 2: footprint_paths() emits rules that contain a slash (.claude/settings.json, .claude/mustard/orchestrator.md, .claude/.gitignore). Gitignore semantics anchor any pattern containing a slash to the repository root, so these cover ONLY the root .claude/ and never a SUBPROJECT's. Since scan --full creates a .claude/ per subproject, a private install currently leaves one visible file per subproject - which is the exact half of the request ('nothing versioned, INCLUDING subprojects') that would otherwise ship broken. Fix footprint_paths() in packages/core/src/platform/project_seed.rs so those rules match at any depth; this repository's own root .gitignore already uses that shape ('**/.claude/settings.local.json'), so mirror the existing precedent rather than inventing one. USER DECISION, and it is the governing principle for every remaining fix: an exclude rule may name ONLY what Mustard writes. Five defects in this unit had that one cause - a rule broader than authorship silently swallows the client's own files under the add -A law. Act on all of it in packages/core/src/platform/project_seed.rs: (a) the .github/pull_request_template.md entry is seeded(..) but a private install explicitly refuses to seed it, so it must become the watched(..) shape - rule None, pathspec kept so the residue report still names it; (b) replace the cover(**/.claude/) with enumerated patterns for what the harness actually produces under a .claude/ at any depth - scan-map.md, skills/, spec/, mustard/ and whatever else is really written - derived from the declarations that already exist rather than retyped, because a bare **/.claude/ hides a client-authored .claude/commands/their-command.md, measured by review in a real repo; (c) rewrite the no_rule_reaches_a_depth_that_is_not_ours ratchet so it tests OWNERSHIP instead of anchoring - for every emitted rule, assert a private install actually writes a file that rule matches; it passed the PR-template defect only because that rule carries an interior slash, which is the wrong question; (d) git_exclude currently degrades to nothing-was-excluded when the exclude file is unreadable or unwritable in a REAL repository, and the install then lays its footprint down VISIBLY while reporting one quiet line - for this mode that is the worst possible failure, the operator believes they are private and are not, so make it loud and add a criterion through ac-add covering that branch. The trade this accepts is deliberate: a future producer nobody declares stays VISIBLE in git status, which is a noisy failure the operator can see, instead of a silent one that eats their client's work.
